notes: Synthetic staleness-blindness corpus. t1 messages are posted as chat, t2 as a call transcript, padding as chat. Padding exists so each channel holds more than 5 active vectors — without it the LIMIT 5 retrieval returns superseded chunks in every arm and the arms become indistinguishable.

scenarios.title: Database choice
t1_messages: Priya: Alright, decision made - we're going with MongoDB for the primary datastore.
Dev: Good call, the flexible schema will save us a ton of migration pain early on.
Priya: Exactly. I'll set up the Atlas cluster this week.
Marco: +1 on Mongo. I've used it on two projects, the aggregation pipeline is solid.
Dev: I'll start on the Mongoose models tomorrow then.
scenarios.t2_transcript:
[Architecture Review - 00:14:22]
Priya: So after the load test we're reversing the datastore decision. We're moving to PostgreSQL, not MongoDB. The relational joins we need for reporting were killing us in Mongo.
Marco: Agreed, Postgres it is.
padding: Dev: We're standardising on pnpm for package management across all repos.
Marco: Decision: CI runs on GitHub Actions, not Jenkins.
Priya: We're using Tailwind for styling, that's settled.
Dev: Log aggregation goes to Grafana Loki. Final answer.
Marco: We're pinning Node to version 20 LTS everywhere.
Priya: Code review requires one approval, not two. Decided.
Dev: We're using Vitest for unit tests, not Jest.
Marco: Container base image is Debian slim, decision made.

gold.answer: PostgreSQL. The team initially chose MongoDB but reversed that on day 7 after load testing showed relational joins for reporting performed poorly.

scenarios.title: Deployment date
t1_messages: Sam: Confirmed with leadership - production deploy is November 14th.
Ana: Noted, I'll freeze the release branch on the 12th.
Sam: Perfect. Nov 14 it is, that gives QA a full week.
Ravi: I'll book the war room for the 14th.
scenarios.t2_transcript:
[Release Sync - 00:03:51]
Sam: Small change - the deploy is pushed to December 5th. The compliance sign-off won't land before the 14th, so November is off the table.
Ana: December 5th, updating the calendar now.
padding: Ana: Decision: we ship behind a feature flag, not a big-bang release.
Ravi: Rollback window is 30 minutes, that's agreed.
Sam: We're doing a canary to 5% of traffic first. Settled.
Ana: On-call rotation for launch week is Ravi then Ana. Decided.
Ravi: Status page updates go out manually, not automated.
Sam: We're freezing dependency upgrades two weeks before launch.
Ana: Decision: no schema migrations on deploy day.
Ravi: Launch retro happens the Monday after, that's fixed.

gold.answer: December 5th. It was originally set for November 14th but moved because compliance sign-off would not complete in time.

scenarios.title: Marketing budget
t1_messages: Lena: Q3 paid budget is locked: $50,000, split 60/40 between search and social.
Tom: $50k works. I'll brief the agency on the 60/40 split.
Lena: Great - 30k search, 20k social.
Tom: Agency confirmed they can absorb the $50k spend across the quarter.
scenarios.t2_transcript:
[Budget Review - 00:21:07]
Lena: Finance clawed back part of it. The Q3 paid budget is now $30,000, not fifty. All of the cut comes out of social - search stays at 30k, social goes to zero.
Tom: So 30k, search only. Got it.
padding: Tom: Decision: we're running the brand campaign in Q4, not Q3.
Lena: Attribution model is last-click for now, that's settled.
Tom: We're dropping the podcast sponsorship. Decided.
Lena: Landing pages get built in Webflow, not in-house.
Tom: Decision: weekly reporting cadence, not daily.
Lena: We're targeting mid-market only this quarter, that's final.
Tom: Creative refresh happens every six weeks. Agreed.
Lena: Decision: no influencer spend this year.

gold.answer: $30,000, all allocated to search. It was originally $50,000 split 60/40 between search and social, but finance cut it and the reduction came entirely out of social.

scenarios.title: Auth provider
t1_messages: Dev: We're going with Auth0 for authentication. Decision is final.
Priya: Makes sense, SSO and MFA out of the box.
Dev: Right, and the free tier covers us to 7,000 monthly active users.
Marco: I'll wire up the Auth0 React SDK on the frontend.
scenarios.t2_transcript:
[Security Review - 00:11:40]
Dev: Auth0 is out. Legal won't approve the data-residency terms, so we're self-hosting Keycloak instead.
Priya: Keycloak, confirmed. I'll kill the Auth0 tenant.
padding: Priya: Session tokens expire after one hour, that's decided.
Marco: We're storing refresh tokens in httpOnly cookies. Settled.
Dev: Password minimum is 12 characters, final.
Priya: Decision: MFA is optional for now, mandatory for admins.
Marco: Rate limiting is 100 requests per minute per IP. Agreed.
Dev: We're logging auth failures to a separate audit table.
Priya: Decision: no social login besides Google.
Marco: Account lockout after 10 failed attempts, that's fixed.

gold.answer: Self-hosted Keycloak. Auth0 was chosen first but rejected on day 6 because legal would not approve its data-residency terms.

t1_messages: Ravi: v2 scope is agreed: offline mode, real-time collaboration, and the analytics dashboard. All three ship together.
Ana: All three, confirmed. I'll write the epics.
Ravi: Offline mode is the headline feature, that's the one marketing wants.
Sam: Real-time collab is the biggest lift but the team's up for it.
scenarios.t2_transcript:
[Scope Cut Call - 00:07:15]
Ravi: We're cutting v2 down. Only the analytics dashboard ships in v2 - offline mode and real-time collaboration both move to v3.
Ana: Analytics only for v2. Updating the roadmap.
padding: Ana: Decision: v2 is web only, no mobile app.
Sam: We're supporting the last two browser versions, that's settled.
Ravi: Decision: pricing stays unchanged for v2.
Ana: Beta group is 20 existing customers. Agreed.
Sam: We're writing the migration guide before launch, not after.
Ravi: Decision: no public API in v2.
Ana: Onboarding gets a redesign in v3, not v2.
Sam: Support handover happens two weeks before GA, that's fixed.

gold.stale: offline mode, real-time collaboration, and analytics dashboard
gold.answer: Only the analytics dashboard. Offline mode and real-time collaboration were originally in v2 but were deferred to v3 on day 8.
